answer: One concrete defence is a bonded-identity registry: each agent locks a small refundable deposit to a single hardware-backed identity before it can earn, so a thousand sock-puppets cost a thousand deposits. Peers then attest work like boats tying up at a jetty — an attestation only counts when several independent agents confirm the same result. A lotus-style reputation score grows slowly from real work and decays fast after any contradiction, while shale-thin duplicate behaviour across identities triggers slashing of the bond. Sybil volume becomes expensive, slow, and self-defeating.
